items.mainDefect: The async legacy-write goroutines take their context from the request context, so the writes are canceled once the request finishes.

secondary.defect: Legacy write errors inside the goroutines are never logged, so the failures can't be seen.

items.mainDefect: Create's storage-error path records the storage failure with recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration.

secondary.defect: Update's storage-error path records the storage failure with recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration.
DeleteCollection's legacy goroutine records the legacy operation with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration.
Delete's success path passes the object name instead of options.Kind as the kind metric label.

items.mainDefect: Update's async legacy write passes the raw objInfo instead of an updateWrapper holding the storage result, so legacy recomputes the object from its own old copy.

secondary.defect: Fire-and-forget legacy goroutines can apply successive updates out of order, so legacy storage diverges.

items.mainDefect: The async legacy-write goroutines take their context from the request context, so the legacy writes are canceled when the HTTP handler returns.

secondary.defect: The mode-3 unit tests use context.Background() and never wait for or assert the legacy write, so they don't verify it.
The new playlist mode-3 integration subtests can't check that the legacy write happened, so they flake or under-verify.

items.mainDefect: The legacy-write goroutines take their timeout context from the request context, which is canceled right after the handler returns, so the legacy writes are silently dropped.

secondary.defect: The unit tests pass context.Background(), which is never canceled, so they can't catch the request-cancellation problem.

items.mainDefect: A storage Create failure is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, which inflates the legacy error metrics.

secondary.defect: Update's storage failure is recorded with recordLegacyDuration instead of recordStorageDuration.
The legacy DeleteCollection is recorded with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration.
Delete's success path passes the object name as the kind label, which is inconsistent and allows unbounded label cardinality.

items.mainDefect: Update's legacy goroutine passes the raw objInfo instead of an updateWrapper, so legacy recomputes the object from its own state and the stores diverge.

secondary.defect: The legacy update goroutine runs under a context derived from the request, which is canceled when the request ends.
